summary: Iceland is a Schengen member state; its Directorate of Immigration describes the Schengen agreement as a partnership between 29 states. EEA/EFTA citizens visiting Iceland must carry valid travel documents or identity cards accepted for border crossing. Other visitors must have a valid visa unless they are exempt from the visa requirement or hold a residence permit issued by another EEA/EFTA country; nationals on the EU's visa-exempt list are exempt for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period (ETIAS is not yet in operation). The visa application fee is EUR 90. Icelandic embassies issue visas in four cities; in about 120 other cities other Schengen states issue visas on Iceland's behalf.

notes: Iceland Revenue and Customs says travellers may import duty-free up to 10 kg of food, including candy, not exceeding the value of ISK 25,000, and are not allowed to import meat and dairy products from outside the European Economic Area.

Iceland Revenue and Customs gives examples of possible duty-free alcohol combinations, such as 1 litre of spirits, 0.75 litre of wine and 3 litres of beer, or 18 litres of beer; the tobacco allowance is 200 cigarettes or 250 g of other tobacco products. The minimum age for bringing alcoholic beverages into Iceland is 20 years, and 18 years for tobacco.

Iceland Revenue and Customs says angling gear and riding clothing used outside Iceland may be brought in if it has been disinfected according to valid regulations; a certificate of disinfection issued by an authorised veterinary officer is accepted, and without one the gear has to be disinfected at the owner's own cost on arrival. Importing used riding gear, including saddles, bridles, halters and whips of leather, is prohibited.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the weather can change quickly and make driving conditions challenging, that some roads, such as in the highlands or interior roads, require 4-wheel drive, and that river levels can change quickly, even within the same day. Canada's travel advice links to road and weather information from the Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration and Safe Travel Iceland.

The UK Foreign Office says the weather can cause damage to rental cars that is not covered by insurance: strong winds are common and can throw sand or ash up, damaging paintwork, and British tourists have had to pay large amounts of money to repair such damage to hire cars.

If you arrive at a Schengen border crossing point for the first time since the EES started, passport control officers will take a photo of your face and/or scan your fingerprints. The EU says the ETIAS travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers is currently not in operation.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Iceland?
faq.answer: EEA/EFTA citizens visiting Iceland must carry valid travel documents or identity cards accepted for border crossing. Nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation 2018/1806), which includes the United States, are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. Other visitors must have a valid visa unless they hold a residence permit issued by another EEA/EFTA country; the visa application fee is EUR 90, and in about 120 cities other Schengen states issue visas on Iceland's behalf.

faq.question: Is Iceland in the Schengen Area even though it is not in the EU?
faq.answer: Yes. Iceland's Directorate of Immigration says Iceland is a Schengen member state, that the Schengen agreement is a partnership between 29 states, and that a uniform visa issued by all Schengen states is valid for travel throughout the region. The Schengen Borders Code sets short stays at no more than 90 days in any 180-day period on the territory of the Schengen states.

faq.question: Do I need ETIAS to visit Iceland?
faq.answer: Not yet. The EU says ETIAS, the new travel authorisation for visa-exempt travellers to enter 30 European countries including Iceland, is currently not in operation and no applications are being collected, and that it will announce the start date several months before launch. The ETIAS website lists a EUR 20 application fee.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for an Icelandair or PLAY stopover in Iceland?
faq.answer: Iceland's Directorate of Immigration says that under the Schengen rules, transit means only a transit from a flight from a non-Schengen state through an airport in a Schengen state and onwards to another non-Schengen state. A person travelling from New York to Iceland and onwards to Berlin, or any other airport in the Schengen area, is not in transit and is entering the Schengen area in Iceland. Citizens of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, the People's Republic of Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia and Sri Lanka need an Airport Transit Visa to transit through an Icelandic airport.

faq.question: Is it safe to drive in Iceland in winter?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says driving can be hazardous, particularly in winter; that winter tires are mandatory between November and April, with exact dates subject to change based on weather conditions; and that roads in the highlands and other remote areas are only open during the summer. It links to road and weather information from the Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration and Safe Travel Iceland.
